card.name: Words just before enzyme or muscle terms
card.fires_on: Small linking words (and, or, of, were, as) or a partial word right before a lab-enzyme or muscle-injury term, such as ALT, myopathy, rhabdomyolysis, ketogenic or karyotype.

modes.label: Linking word before lab or muscle term
modes.description: A short connector such as and, or, of, as sits just before an enzyme or muscle-damage term.
modes.example: Quinine may increase plasma concentrations of atorvastatin, thereby increasing the risk of myopathy<< or>> rhabdomyolysis.

modes.label: Start of a medical word
modes.description: The first piece of a long medical term whose next piece begins with k or similar.
modes.example: The diagnosis can be confirmed by a test called a<< k>>aryotype.

card.writes: It seems to push the next word toward an enzyme, muscle or lab-test term and away from words starting with v or va.
card.plain: It lights up on the small word just before a lab enzyme or muscle-injury term is about to appear.
